key_insight: Introducing learned global scene tokens that provide scene-level awareness to a feed-forward Gaussian splatting pipeline, enabling efficient, compact allocation of 3D Gaussians without slow iterative optimization.
problem_solved: Current Gaussian-splatting methods either rely on slow iterative optimization or local heuristics that produce suboptimal allocation of primitives, forcing a trade-off between representation compactness, reconstruction fidelity, and rendering speed.
method: Encode an input scene into a small set of global scene tokens that capture global structure and importance.
Use a feed-forward decoder that conditions Gaussian primitive allocation (positions, scales, colors, confidences) on the global tokens to allocate primitives globally-aware and compactly.
Apply lightweight pruning/aggregation and reconstruction losses so the network produces a fast, high-fidelity Gaussian-splatting representation suitable for real-time rendering.
impact: Enables practitioners to obtain high-quality 3D reconstructions with far fewer primitives and much faster inference than iterative methods, making Gaussian-splatting practical for real-time, large-scale, or resource-constrained applications.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: image(s) → encoder → global scene tokens → feed-forward Gaussian allocator → rendered output
Before vs after comparison: dense iterative allocation vs GlobalSplat compact allocation (primitives count + visual difference)
Speed vs quality chart: rendering latency on x-axis, reconstruction error or PSNR on y-axis, showing GlobalSplat Pareto improvement
Sample renders and close-ups: ground-truth photo, GlobalSplat render, and error heatmap
paper_title: GlobalSplat: Efficient Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting via Global Scene Tokens
paper_authors: Roni Itkin, Noam Issachar, Yehonatan Keypur, Yehonatan Keypur, Anpei Chen
